greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Grace and peace be with you all as we gather in the presence of our merciful God.
penitential:
Lord Jesus, you are our shield and our fortress. Lord, have mercy.
Christ Jesus, you gather us under the shadow of your wings. Christ, have mercy.
Lord Jesus, you lead us safely to the banquet of heaven. Lord, have mercy.
psalm_response: Blessed be the Lord, my Rock!
homily:
We begin today not with a grand theological argument, but with the quiet sound of armor being strapped into place in the dark. St. Paul tells the Ephesians to put on the belt of truth, to buckle the breastplate of righteousness, to lace their feet with the readiness of the Gospel of peace. It is an image of preparation, of standing your ground when the wind begins to blow cold and the day feels heavy. Think of the simple, physical reality of getting ready for the morning. A boy standing in the hallway, checking his shoes, adjusting his jacket, stepping out the door into the morning light with a backpack full of questions and a mind that is already racing toward the horizon. He is getting ready for whatever the day holds.

I want you to hold onto that single image: the belt of truth, the gear worn for a journey. It is the image of a traveler getting ready to move.

Now, let us tell the truth before we try to comfort ourselves. Alan, Thao, Ryan, and everyone gathered here in this sacred space or tuning in from afar, carrying the quiet, crushing weight of a missing presence: we know what it is like to stand in a hallway that is too quiet. We know what it is like to wake up and feel the day pressing down on you before you have even opened your eyes. Four months have passed since Benjamin Vo went home to God, and the silence in your home does not ask for polite answers. It asks for honesty. You look at the places where he used to be—the quiet corners, the spaces filled with his bright curiosity, the brilliant logic of a boy who loved the mechanics of flight and the vastness of the skies—and the ache is real. It is an ache that does not leave room for cheap clichés. It is heavy. It is wearying. It makes you wonder how to stand firm when the ground beneath your feet feels shaken.

There is a temptation, when life breaks our hearts, to look backward through a lens of quiet self-blame. We search the past for missed signs. We wonder if we could have done something differently, if we could have stood watch more carefully, if some hidden detail slipped through our fingers. Let us lift that stone from your hearts right now. You missed nothing. You were the parents, the family, the brother Benjamin was given. You loved him with a completeness that filled his fifteen years with joy, with travel across the world, with the sweet warmth of shared stories and laughter. God does not accuse you, and you must not accuse yourselves. Some sorrows in this fragile world arrive entirely beyond human reach, untouched by anything anyone did or failed to do. You are not to blame. Let that heavy stone fall to the ground, and let your shoulders rest.

And then, right into the middle of that ache, the Gospel breaks in like light coming under a closed door. Jesus stands looking over Jerusalem, a city that breaks his heart, and he says something astonishing. He does not threaten or condemn. He says: 'How many times I yearned to gather your children together as a hen gathers her brood under her wings, but you were unwilling!' Think of that image. The wings. The warmth. The fierce, gentle protection of a mother bird pulling her little ones close against the storm. Jesus is not a distant judge sitting in the clouds; he is the One who opens his wings and pulls you under them. He covers you when the wind is bitter. He holds you when the night is long.

Benjamin knew about wings and flight. He was a boy who looked at the sky with wonder, who dreamed of airlines and soaring high above the earth, who giggled with pure joy when he talked about 'con chim airlines.' He had that brilliant, sharp mind—the mind that mastered complex systems and mathematics years ahead of his time—yet his heart was always gentle, always turned toward others. Think of the time he offered his entire piggy bank, unprompted, simply because an uncle was hurting. He didn't need to break it open; the offer itself revealed the magnificent, generous soul God had placed inside him. That is the boy you raised. That is the boy who walked beside you on your journeys, from the busy streets of distant cities to the quiet moments at home.

And now, Benjamin is soaring. He is at the banquet of heaven, resting in the light of the Father, standing alongside kindred spirits like the young Saint Carlo Acutis. He is home. And from that place of eternal peace, he is watching over you. Just as he once shared his smile and his sweetness with everyone around him, his memory is now a wellspring of grace. Think of the clean water flowing in Cà Mau, Vietnam, from the well dedicated in his name—the 'Great Ocean' of his middle name poured out to quench the thirst of the poor. His love did not stop when his breathing stopped. It keeps moving. It keeps giving. It keeps blessing the earth.

Alan, Thao, Ryan, you are still a family of four. Death cannot sever what God has joined in love. When you feel the quiet of the house, remember that you are wrapped in the very wings of Christ. He is holding Benjamin, and he is holding you. He is whispering to your hearts that love is stronger than the grave, and that the story is not finished.

So what do you carry out the door today? Not a heavy burden, but one small, doable thing: when the grief rises and the hallway feels empty, pause, close your eyes, and imagine the shadow of those wings. Let yourself be gathered. Trust that you are held. And walk out into the day with the quiet, unshakeable hope that the one you love is waiting for you in the light, smiling, and completely at peace.
standing_petitions: For Benjamin, and for all who have gone before us marked with the sign of faith, that they now rest in the radiant light of Christ's presence, we pray to the Lord.
For Alan, Thao, Ryan, and all who carry the heavy cross of grief, that the Lord wrap them in his gentle wings and fill their hearts with his enduring hope, we pray to the Lord.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot now receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, make his face shine upon you and be gracious to you, and give you his peace, now and forever. Amen.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
Brothers and sisters:
Draw your strength from the Lord and from his mighty power.
Put on the armor of God so that you may be able to stand firm
against the tactics of the Devil.
For our struggle is not with flesh and blood
but with the principalities, with the powers,
with the world rulers of this present darkness,
with the evil spirits in the heavens.
Therefore, put on the armor of God,
that you may be able to resist on the evil day
and, having done everything, to hold your ground.
So stand fast with your loins girded in truth,
clothed with righteousness as a breastplate,
and your feet shod in readiness for the Gospel of peace.
In all circumstances, hold faith as a shield,
to quench all the flaming arrows of the Evil One.
And take the helmet of salvation and the sword of the Spirit,
which is the word of God.With all prayer and supplication,
pray at every opportunity in the Spirit.
To that end, be watchful with all perseverance and supplication
for all the holy ones and also for me,
that speech may be given me to open my mouth,
to make known with boldness the mystery of the Gospel
for which I am an ambassador in chains,
so that I may have the courage to speak as I must.

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
R. (1b) Blessed be the Lord, my Rock!
Blessed be the LORD, my rock,
who trains my hands for battle, my fingers for war.
R. Blessed be the Lord, my Rock!
My mercy and my fortress,
my stronghold, my deliverer,
My shield, in whom I trust,
who subdues my people under me.
R. Blessed be the Lord, my Rock!
O God, I will sing a new song to you;
with a ten-stringed lyre I will chant your praise,
You who give victory to kings,
and deliver David, your servant from the evil sword.
R. Blessed be the Lord, my Rock!

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
Some Pharisees came to Jesus and said,
“Go away, leave this area because Herod wants to kill you.”
He replied, “Go and tell that fox,
‘Behold, I cast out demons and I perform healings today and tomorrow,
and on the third day I accomplish my purpose.
Yet I must continue on my way today, tomorrow, and the following day,
for it is impossible that a prophet should die
outside of Jerusalem.’“Jerusalem, Jerusalem,
you who kill the prophets and stone those sent to you,
how many times I yearned to gather your children together
as a hen gathers her brood under her wings,
but you were unwilling!
Behold, your house will be abandoned.
But I tell you, you will not see me until the time comes when you say,
Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.”

day: Thursday of the Thirtieth Week in Ordinary Time

pet_prayers.text: Thinking of you buddy! Stop by to say hello whenever you can okay? Love you Ben

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - Been dreaming about you a lot. Hope you're having fun up in heaven. Please look after our family. Remember to come say hi daily. We miss you so much!

Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. Xin Chúa thương nhậm lời Ben, cho Ben được hưởng ngàn thu bình an bên Chúa. Nếu có thể, xin Ben lại ghé thăm anh trong những giấc mơ tiếp theo nhé, dù chỉ là một lời chào hay một nụ cười thân thương như ngày nào.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever

Quỷ nhỏ, tự nhiên nghĩ về mày buồn dễ sợ. Hãy đi đến những nơi mà Ben muốn nha và đừng quên là luôn nhớ về gia đình mình nhé, thương em trai nhiều. Giá như !!!!!!!!!

pet_prayers.text: What happened my son? It's been 3 months since you left us. Missing you so much my whole body aches. Mom cries every day now... What are we going to do now Ben?  Please pray for us.
